facts: **$A = 2\pi r^{2} + 2\pi rh$** for a **closed** cylinder, where $r$ is the radius and $h$ is the perpendicular height.
The formula uses the **radius**, so halve a given diameter before substituting.
Keep the working exact and round only on the last line.
A multiple of $\pi$ such as $104\pi$ cm² is the **exact** area, while a rounded decimal is written with $\approx$.
Surface area is measured in **square** units, so lengths in centimetres give an area in cm².
steps: Substitute the radius (halving a given diameter first) and the height.
Evaluate, then round or leave in terms of $\pi$ as asked.

workedExamples.solution_text:
The two circular ends have total area $2\pi r^{2}$.
The curved side unrolls into a rectangle with length $2\pi r$ and width $h$, so its area is $2\pi rh$.
Adding the three faces gives $A=2\pi r^{2}+2\pi rh$.

Halve the diameter to find the radius.
$\begin{aligned}r&=\frac{14}{2}=7\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}A&=2\pi r^{2}+2\pi rh\\&=2\pi(7)^{2}+2\pi(7)(9)\\&=98\pi+126\pi\\&=224\pi\text{ cm}^{2}\\&\approx703.7\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Closed cylinder A has radius $6$ cm and height $4$ cm. Closed cylinder B has radius $4$ cm and height $6$ cm. Which has the larger total surface area? Justify your answer using exact areas.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Cylinder A:
$\begin{aligned}A&=2\pi r^{2}+2\pi rh\\&=2\pi(6)^{2}+2\pi(6)(4)\\&=72\pi+48\pi\\&=120\pi\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$
Cylinder B:
$\begin{aligned}A&=2\pi r^{2}+2\pi rh\\&=2\pi(4)^{2}+2\pi(4)(6)\\&=32\pi+48\pi\\&=80\pi\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$
Cylinder A has the larger surface area because $120\pi>80\pi$.

workedExamples.question_text: A cylinder has radius $7$ cm and curved surface area $168\pi$ cm². Find its height.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Use the curved surface area $2\pi rh$.
$\begin{aligned}2\pi rh&=168\pi\\2\pi(7)h&=168\pi\\14\pi h&=168\pi\\h&=12\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A closed cylinder has radius $5$ m and total surface area $400$ m². Find its height to $1$ decimal place.

workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}2\pi x^{2}+2\pi x(4x)&=160\pi\\2\pi x^{2}+8\pi x^{2}&=160\pi\\10\pi x^{2}&=160\pi\\x^{2}&=16\\x&=4\end{aligned}$
Take the positive square root because the radius is a positive length.

A closed cylinder has a radius of $4$ cm and a height of $10$ cm.
A second closed cylinder has a radius of $5$ cm and a height of $6$ cm.
Find both surface areas in exact form in terms of $\pi$, and state which cylinder has the greater surface area.
development.solution_text:
First cylinder: $A = 2\pi(4)^{2} + 2\pi(4)(10)$
$= 32\pi + 80\pi$
$= 112\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$
Second cylinder: $A = 2\pi(5)^{2} + 2\pi(5)(6)$
$= 50\pi + 60\pi$
$= 110\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$
The first cylinder has the greater surface area, since $112\pi > 110\pi$.
